beats.narration_text: Hi — I'm Sudhanva, with this week's STEM explainer for the RL Environments project. One score for the whole team: how do four ants split it?

props.command: Open our trained VDN and QMIX ants and show me how one team value gets split among four ants.
output: VDN: team value = sum of 4 ant values (12.616 at this state)
QMIX mixing weights at this state: 160 of 160 are ≥ 0
1,296 joint moves scored on 29,922 states: own picks always score top

beats.narration_text: Train on one team score, then let each ant pick alone. By design, the ants' own best moves together score the team's best.

props.text:
Train on one team score
then pick every move centrally

beats.narration_text: VDN is the simple version: the team's value is the sum of four ant values. In this real moment, each ant rates its six moves, and the team value is the four best ratings, added.

shot.new_visual_element: MathTex Q_tot = Σ_i Q_i(o_i, a_i); real held-out state (episode 10,000, t=25: ants 2 and 4 holding a piece); 4×6 table of VDN Q-values with each ant's best boxed; Q_tot = 1.753 + 3.696 + 3.612 + 3.555 = 12.616
shot.visual_intent: SHOW: evidence probe.frame + probe.vdn.q / q_greedy / q_tot_best

show.event: MathTex Q_tot = Σ Q_i writes on (Sunehag et al. 2018)
the real grid state draws, ants numbered 1–4
4 × 6 table of Q-values fills row by row (stay · N · S · E · W · work)
each row's maximum boxed: south 1.753 · east 3.696 · west 3.612 · east 3.555
the four boxed values slide into 1.753 + 3.696 + 3.612 + 3.555 = 12.616

beats.narration_text: QMIX swaps the sum for a small network. Its weights come from networks that read the whole map, and they're never negative — so raising one ant's value can never lower the team's.

shot.new_visual_element: Mixer diagram: four Q_i → |W1| (4×32) → ELU → |w2| (32) → Q_tot, with hypernetworks reading the 517-number state; the 160 real mixing weights at the same state as bars, all above the zero line (min 0.015); ∂Q_tot/∂Q_i = 1.20 · 1.07 · 0.75 · 1.28
shot.visual_intent: SHOW: antrl/algos/networks.py QMixer (torch.abs on hyper_w1 / hyper_w2) + evidence probe.qmix.mixing

beats.narration_text: Now check it. Four ants, six moves each: one thousand two hundred ninety-six joint moves. Score them all, and the one built from each ant's own pick always gets the top score — on nearly thirty thousand states.

shot.new_visual_element: 36 × 36 grid of all 1,296 joint moves shaded by VDN's Q_tot at the probe state; the per-ant pick marked and the top cell lighting up on it; counter 29,922 of 29,922 states (6 saved models × 50 held-out episodes) where the own-pick joint move scores the top Q_tot

beats.narration_text: On the grid, VDN carries pieces home: five and a half of twelve units of food. The best QMIX run climbed to three point eight six, then fell to near zero.
